artifacts.synopsis: RE Glen Mapes appealed his conviction and censures by a temporary session of New Hope Christian Church. The SJC sustained the appeal in part, affirming the finding that he failed to submit to church government but reversing the excessive suspension and deposition and replacing them with admonition; the related complaint was moot after the church left the PCA.

artifacts.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.synopsis: Steven Hahn challenged Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery's handling of complaints arising from Christ the King's restriction on his attendance while he sought a psychiatric evaluation. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session's action was pastoral guidance rather than judicial censure and that no clear error was shown in the lower courts' judgment.

artifacts.title: Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in dismissing TE Eliot Lee's charges against two Teaching Elders without conducting a trial; the SJC held that once properly drawn charges are filed, a Presbytery must proceed to adjudicate them unless it can demonstrate specific constitutional grounds for dismissal, and remanded the matter to KEP.
